entities.summary:
Flaithbertach mac Loingsig was a High King of Ireland, ruling from 728 to 734. He was the son of Loingsech mac Óengusso, a previous high king, and a member of the Cenél Conaill, a branch of the northern Uí Néill. His reign was marked by the expansion of Irish power and influence, as well as the continued struggle against the Viking raids. Despite this, his legacy was largely overshadowed by that of his successors, who would go on to shape the course of Irish history in the centuries to come.

This reign was also significant for the development of Irish law and governance, as Flaithbertach implemented various reforms and established a more centralized state. Furthermore, his reign was marked by the continued importance of the Church in Irish society, with many monasteries and churches being built or restored during this period.

In the end, Flaithbertach mac Loingsig's reign was cut short by his death in 765 CE, but his impact on Irish history was lasting.

Flaithbertach mac Loingsig was a key figure in the struggle for power and influence in medieval Ireland, and his legacy continues to be felt today.

The high king's reign was marked by a series of significant events, including the Battle of Magh Rath, which took place in 731 CE. This battle was a major turning point in the struggle between the Irish and the Vikings, and it had a lasting impact on the course of Irish history.

Despite the significance of his reign, Flaithbertach mac Loingsig's legacy is somewhat overshadowed by that of his successors, who would go on to shape the course of Irish history in the centuries to come.
